[RFCS.19.1] The framing is two levels and both are protobuf. A container is a
`Dsc` or a `Stream`, each declared `repeated Atom atoms = 1`
(`proto/atom.proto#Dsc`, `proto/atom.proto#Stream`). So the unit repeated on the wire is
the **outer frame** — `[0x0A][varint len][Atom]`, the field-1 tag of the container message
— and the **inner** `Atom` is itself `[tag][varint len][body]`, where that tag is the
atom's oneof field number and carries its identity ([RFCS.16.1]).

```ebnf
container   = { frame } ;                  (* Dsc or Stream; type from the first atom *)
frame       = outer_tag , varint_len , atom ;
outer_tag   = %x0A ;                       (* field 1, wire type 2 *)
atom        = oneof_tag , varint_len , body ;
oneof_tag   = ?varint of (field_number << 3 | 2)? ;
```

**Residue the grammar cannot carry ([STYL.2.15.4]):** `outer_tag` is one byte for every
atom. A partial trailing `frame` is EOF ([RFCS.19.2]); the productions
cannot say that. And the container's *type* is not in the grammar at all: it is the first
atom's field number ([RFCS.19.4]).
